chapter: Ben Pollack band and New York
title: Teagarden joins the Pollack band; Miller steps aside
summary: Pollack and Gil Rodin hire Teagarden and Miller gracefully becomes arranger, leaving a front line of Goodman, Teagarden and McPartland.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: And so what happened then was after a few days Ben Pollack and Gil Rodin who was more or less the manager/decided that they wanted Jack Teagarden and Glenn Miller gracefully bowed out and said well I'll do the arranging and let Jack come in on trombone.

Yes. He said I'll be the arranger which was what he was doing anyway, and it will give me more time to arrange and Jack came in on trombone. So we had a small band, see it was eleven, twelve piece band that we had, the Pollack band. He even had a couple of fiddles in there and a cello (shuttle?). At the Park Central Hotel that was. So Jack came with the band, Glen did the arranging and we had a great small band. We used to have the small band come out in front and you know when we played jam numbers, jam you know, no music to that, no arrangements, just ..... So we had a good front line there. Benny Goodman and Jack Teagarden and Jimmy McPartland on the cornet. (LAUGHTER).
